lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: Tapping Confirm change mutates only view-local decision state and immediately renders a receipt saying Relationship state confirmed; the frozen source contains no authoritative write, reconciliation, revision, or receipt payload on this path.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:11 and :61-80 set @State decision to .confirmed, while :461-495 render Relationship state confirmed; apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift:23-49 asserts only that this local receipt appears.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can believe the relationship record was committed when only the current presentation changed; leaving or relaunching can silently discard the decision and undermine trust in later work.
findings.recommendation: Drive confirmation through an authoritative proposal command with revision and idempotency identifiers; show confirming, failed, conflict, and unknown-locked states, and render confirmed only from a reconciled structured receipt.
findings.verification: On the frozen successor build, confirm once under success, response loss, timeout, offline transition, backgrounding, termination, and relaunch; the UI must never show confirmed before reconciliation, must preserve context, and exactly one canonical revision and receipt must exist.

findings.observation: The Today surface remains relationship-first rather than Pursuit-first: it names Leila and a search plus an unresolved issue, but omits the target outcome, deadline, current milestone, and explicit goal-level reason that make the priority comparable.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 screenshot docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-baseline/ios-today-light.png; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:170-271; frozen Decision Draft v2.0 sections 6.1 and 7.1 require Today to lead with Pursuit, Gap/Action, Goal, evidence freshness, and one primary action.
findings.user_impact: The recruiter can see what changed for one person but cannot identify the target outcome that deserves attention or compare why this work should move now.
findings.recommendation: Make each Today focus start with Pursuit outcome, deadline or milestone, blocking gap, evidence freshness, and one scoped action; retain the person as a role-bearing resource inside that goal context.
findings.verification: Run first-use task testing on the revised Today screen; at least 9 of 10 recruiters must correctly state the target outcome, blocker, evidence freshness, and next action within 10 seconds without opening another screen.

findings.observation: The review keeps quote and provenance near the decision, but exposes only whole-package Keep unresolved or Confirm change controls. It provides no visible associated-person correction, field-level edit, item-level reject, or independent confirmation of multiple proposed facts.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:17-93 shows one evidence block, one proposed relationship state, and two package-level decisions; the full name is not rendered in the review body and the toolbar at :111-113 shows only initials; Decision Draft v2.0 section 7.5 and V1-REV-001/002 require source, identity, before, proposed, reason, effect, and per-item confirm/edit/reject/keep unresolved.
findings.user_impact: A seeded OCR, identity, or interpretation error cannot be corrected while retaining valid facts, so the safest option is to abandon or defer the entire review.
findings.recommendation: Render the full associated person and Pursuit with a Change control, split proposed claims into independent rows, and give every row edit, reject, confirm, and keep-unresolved behavior with its own evidence and effect.
findings.verification: Seed a wrong-person association and one incorrect fact among three proposals; 9 of 10 users must correct both errors, retain the two valid proposals, and verify the final receipt without leaving the review.

findings.observation: The frozen Today-to-review implementation is a happy path with local confirmed/unresolved state. It has no loading, stale, conflict, failure, retry, expiry, unknown-outcome, or relaunch-recovery state for this surface, and the frozen test run failed rather than proving the required matrix.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:8-121 models only an optional local decision; apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift:11-49 covers default launch and local receipt only; artifact.json records pnpm ios:check exit 65 with the relationship capture test failed and localhost sync skipped; Decision Draft v2.0 sections 20.1 and 25 require Today and Review state matrices plus all-green deterministic journeys.
findings.user_impact: Interruption, stale data, or an unavailable backend has no truthful state or safe recovery contract on the reviewed path, so work can appear complete, disappear, or invite an unsafe repeat.
findings.recommendation: Implement explicit quiet, stale, partial, offline, confirming, conflict, unknown-locked, applied, and failed states backed by durable identifiers, then cover cancellation, retry, interruption, relaunch, and duplicate suppression.
findings.verification: Execute the complete Today and Review state matrix on a reproducible build; every row must end in a deterministic state, preserve the review context, and produce zero silent loss, false success, or duplicate operation.

findings.observation: The top-level navigation is Today, People, Library, while the frozen design defines Today, Pursuits, People and explicitly says evidence should not be a daily Library tab. The current hierarchy therefore has no direct goal workspace despite the V2 Pursuit-centered success condition.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 screenshot docs/evaluations/2026-08-24-v1-baseline/ios-today-light.png; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:62-80 and :95-168; Decision Draft v2.0 section 6.1 defines Today/Pursuits/People and routes evidence through Pursuit, Person, Review, and Search.
findings.user_impact: Users are steered toward people and evidence storage before they can open the outcome, resource map, gaps, and plan that explain why those records matter.
findings.recommendation: Replace Library in primary navigation with Pursuits, preserve each tab's navigation stack, and expose evidence contextually from Pursuit, Person, Review, and unified Search.
findings.verification: From a cold launch, a recruiter must reach the named Pursuit, identify outcome/milestone/gap, open the supporting evidence, and return without losing tab context; no primary Library tab should be present.

findings.observation: The Guide-to-capture transition dismisses a sheet and waits a fixed 250 ms before presenting the capture workbench, making navigation timing-dependent rather than state-driven.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:37-43 uses Task.sleep(250_000_000); Decision Draft v2.0 section 6.2 requires typed route reduction and forbids fixed-delay navigation.
findings.user_impact: Slow animation, Reduce Motion, backgrounding, or rapid interaction can race the presentation and make Capture fail to appear or appear from stale context.
findings.recommendation: Represent the handoff as one typed navigation transition and present Capture from observed dismissal or route state, without elapsed-time assumptions.
findings.verification: Repeat Guide-to-Capture 50 times under Reduce Motion, rapid taps, background/foreground, and the slowest supported device; every run must open exactly one correctly scoped capture surface with no presentation warning.

strengths: The light-mode screenshot has calm editorial craft, restrained vermilion, readable grouping, and one visually dominant Review change action.
The review source places the exact quote and provenance before the proposed change and explicitly says that no message or external-system write will occur.
The inspected source generally uses relative text styles, vertical fixed sizing, scroll containers, and 44-48 point minimum control heights rather than tiny tap targets.
missing_evidence: No evidence-level-1 executable interaction or accessibility inspection was frozen; confidence is capped at supported_inference.

Only one large-iPhone portrait light screenshot is frozen; small iPhone, landscape, oldest deployment target, dark mode, increased contrast, Reduce Transparency, and Reduce Motion were not shown for Today-to-review.
No Dynamic Type XXXL/AX3/AX5, 200% localization expansion, Simplified Chinese, RTL, or long mixed-script identity evidence was run on the editorial Today and RelationshipChangeReview surfaces.
No VoiceOver linear-order, name/value/hint, grouped-evidence, Full Keyboard Access, Switch Control, or assistive-technology user evidence was frozen for the critical path.

No slow-network, offline, cancellation, stale, conflict, unknown outcome, timeout reconciliation, background, termination, relaunch, or duplicate-write proof exists for the current relationship review.
No measured critical-path latency, main-thread responsiveness, memory, launch budget, or graceful degraded-mode evidence was frozen.
The frozen pnpm ios:check result is failed, so the available tests cannot serve as an all-green release receipt.
vetoes: The review presents an unverified relationship-state write as successful: tapping Confirm changes only view-local state, then renders Relationship state confirmed.
open_questions: What canonical service and revision owns a confirmed relationship change on this path, and what structured receipt will the UI reconcile?
Where in the current build can the recruiter inspect the Pursuit outcome, deadline, milestone, resource map, and closing condition for the surfaced gap?
How will the review surface expose wrong-identity correction and field-level editing without forcing acceptance or rejection of the whole proposal?
